3Q25 Macro Themes:

USA: Inflation’s Re-Acceleration: The distortion bonanza and sensationalist soundbite parade in 1H25 eclipsed only by the profit opportunity available in fading manic rotations in tourist headline chasing in favor of GoAnywhere Macro Risk Management rotations: Quad2/3 (Jan-early Feb) → non-recessionary Quad4 (Feb-Apr) → Quad 2 (May-pres) → “NEXT”. With structural market changes, intensifying geopolitical frictions, rising cycle fragility and the timeline for major macro & policy catalysts all converging, the surface area of risk will continue to expand in 2H25.  We’ll review the why of 1H, detail our expectations around the where “NEXT”,  qualify the asymmetry in the trajectory for inflation nearer-term and review the practical approach to risk managing more rotational chop in the monthly Quads.

Global #Quad2 Remains: While U.S. tariff policy has captured headlines, the broader global economy has quietly sustained its momentum, with Quad 2 conditions remaining intact. International trade did not retreat—it rerouted—allowing countries like Germany, Belgium, Australia, and India to emerge as new beneficiaries of shifting global supply chains. These nations have seized the opportunity to expand their economic footprints, helping drive a sustained growth regime even as traditional industrial powers recalibrate. Meanwhile, a softer U.S. dollar—down 10.5% from its peak at the start of the year—has provided a powerful tailwind and easing financial conditions abroad. As a result, the global macro environment continues to defy stagflationary fears, propelled by favorable FX dynamics and resilient trade flows that reinforce the persistence of growth. We will continue to measure and map the durability of these conditions—and identify precisely when, and if, this global expansion begins to falter.

Policy Impact: Tariffs, Tax Cuts, Stablecoin, etc.: Q3 will mark the in-between period between the adverse 1H25 DOGE/Trade War dynamics and the light at the end of the tunnel Q425/1Q26 Tax Cuts. This will be the period where impacts on growth and inflation will incrementally manifest on both growth and inflation. Moreover, the One Big Beautiful Bill will perpetuate the prevailing condition set of higher Deficits/Debt. Just in time, it would seem, recent developments around Stablecoins and Bank Regulation will create new demand channel incentives for owning Treasuries just as the outlook for Fiscal recklessness gets turbocharged. Understanding the sequencing and effects of these dynamics should be complementary to the underlying baseline of Quads and Signals across both short and intermediate durations.

- Your Macro Team
